Apple___Apple_scab.preparation: Dissolve copper sulfate in 5L of water and lime in another 5L. Pour copper solution into lime solution while stirring continuously.
Apple___Apple_scab.application: Apply during green-tip and pink-bud stages as a protective shield. Spray every 7-10 days in wet spring weather.
Apple___Apple_scab.cause: Venturia inaequalis fungus, overwintering on fallen infected leaves.
Apple___Apple_scab.symptoms: Olive-green to brown velvety spots on leaves and fruit, causing leaf distortion and cracked fruit skin.
Apple___Apple_scab.prevention_methods: Rake and destroy fallen leaves in autumn. Prune tree canopy to maximize sunshine and wind penetration.

chemical_pesticides.name: Captan 50 WP or Myclobutanil
chemical_pesticides.safety_instructions: Wear face mask and safety goggles. Extremely irritating to eyes. 7-day pre-harvest interval.

fertilizer.application_timing: Apply in early spring before bud break.

Apple___Black_rot.preparation: Mix neem oil with soap in warm water to emulsify, then blend in garlic extract and stir thoroughly.
Apple___Black_rot.application: Spray trees every 7-10 days starting at petal fall to protect developing fruit. Apply in the evening.
Apple___Black_rot.cause: Botryosphaeria obtusa fungus, colonizing dead wood, pruned branches, and mummified fruit.
Apple___Black_rot.symptoms: Frog-eye spots on leaves (purple rim, tan center), sunken black cankers on branches, and rotting fruit with concentric black rings.
Apple___Black_rot.prevention_methods: Prune out dead branches and cankers during winter. Remove all mummified apples from the orchard.

chemical_pesticides.name: Thiophanate-methyl or Captan
chemical_pesticides.safety_instructions: Use protective gloves. Do not contaminate garden ponds. Wash clothing worn during spraying separately.

fertilizer.application_timing: Split application: half in early spring, half after fruit harvest.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.preparation: Mix sulfur powder with a little water to form a smooth paste, then dilute into the full volume of water.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.application: Apply at weekly intervals from pink-bud stage until petals fall to disrupt fungal spore germination.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.cause: Gymnosporangium juniperi-virginianae fungus, requiring both cedar/juniper trees and apple trees to complete its life cycle.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.symptoms: Bright yellow-orange spots on leaves with tiny black dots, leading to spore-bearing tubes on leaf undersides and early defoliation.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.prevention_methods: Remove nearby wild red cedars/junipers within a 1-mile radius if possible. Plant rust-resistant varieties.

chemical_pesticides.name: Myclobutanil or Triadimefon
chemical_pesticides.safety_instructions: Harmful if swallowed. Keep out of reach of children and pets. Do not apply when temperature exceeds 30°C.

fertilizer.application_timing: Apply in late autumn to support root resilience through winter.

Apple___healthy.application: Apple tree is healthy. Continue pruning in winter and checking for pests.
Apple___healthy.cause: Optimal tree hygiene and balanced orchard nutrition
Apple___healthy.symptoms: Lush green canopy, clean fruits with smooth skin, and strong branch joints.
Apple___healthy.prevention_methods: Perform yearly winter pruning, paint trunks to protect against sunscald, and maintain insect traps.

chemical_pesticides.name: N/A (Not required)
chemical_pesticides.safety_instructions: None

fertilizer.application_timing: Spread around the drip-line of the tree canopy in late winter.

Blueberry___healthy.application: Blueberry bush is healthy. Maintain acidic soil pH (4.5-5.5) and keep soil evenly moist.
Blueberry___healthy.cause: Optimal soil acidity and well-draining moist conditions
Blueberry___healthy.symptoms: Vibrant green leaves, reddish-brown healthy canes, and abundant blossoms or berries.
Blueberry___healthy.prevention_methods: Apply pine bark or peat moss mulch. Avoid overhead watering to prevent fruit rots.

chemical_pesticides.name: N/A (Not required)

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.preparation: Dissolve potassium bicarbonate and soap thoroughly in water.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.application: Spray foliage thoroughly at first sign of white powdery spots, repeating every 7-10 days in warm dry weather.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.cause: Podosphaera clandestina fungus, favored by warm, dry climates with high relative humidity.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White powdery fungal patches on leaves and young shoots, causing leaves to curl upwards and drop prematurely.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.prevention_methods: Prune interior branches to increase sunlight and airflow. Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilizing.

chemical_pesticides.name: Myclobutanil or Tebuconazole
chemical_pesticides.safety_instructions: Wear eye protection and gloves. Avoid spraying during bloom to protect pollinators. 14-day pre-harvest interval.

fertilizer.application_timing: Spray bi-weekly to strengthen leaf epidermal cell walls.

Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.application: Cherry tree is healthy. Keep soil mulched and maintain routine pruning.
Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.cause: Good airflow and proper orchard care
Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.symptoms: Glossy green leaves, sturdy fruit spurs, and clear spotless bark.
Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.prevention_methods: Prune out crisscrossing branches. Apply dormant oil spray in late winter to suppress overwintering insect pests.

chemical_pesticides.name: N/A (Not required)
chemical_pesticides.safety_instructions: None

fertilizer.application_timing: Apply in early spring as new growth starts.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.preparation: Mix neem oil with soap to emulsify, stir in turmeric powder, then dilute with water.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.application: Spray foliage every 7 days when gray lesions first appear, especially in humid and rainy conditions.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.cause: Cercospora zeae-maydis fungus, surviving in corn residue on the soil surface.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.symptoms: Rectangular, tan to gray lesions with sharp parallel borders confined between leaf veins, causing premature leaf death.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.prevention_methods: Rotate crops with non-grass crops (like soybean). Till corn debris into the soil or practice residue management.

chemical_pesticides.name: Pyraclostrobin + Fluxapyroxad or Azoxystrobin
chemical_pesticides.safety_instructions: Apply at early tasseling stage. Toxic to aquatic life. Wear protective clothing and respirator.

fertilizer.quantity: 25 kg Potash + 10 kg Zinc per acre
fertilizer.application_timing: Apply as basal dose during final soil preparation.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.preparation: Crush garlic, mix with turmeric powder into water, and let steep for 12 hours before straining.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.application: Spray on leaves every 5-7 days at the first sign of rust-colored pustules.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.cause: Puccinia sorghi fungus, spreading via windborne spores in high humidity (90%+).
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.symptoms: Powdery, cinnamon-brown pustules on both upper and lower leaf surfaces, causing leaves to yellow and dry.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.prevention_methods: Plant rust-resistant hybrids, control weed hosts, and destroy infected residues post-harvest.

chemical_pesticides.name: Propiconazole or Pyraclostrobin
chemical_pesticides.safety_instructions: Avoid direct inhalation. Wear chemical-resistant gloves. Protect local water systems from chemical runoff.

fertilizer.application_timing: Side-dress at knee-high growth stage (V6 stage) to help crop withstand stress.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.preparation: Mix neem oil with soap first to emulsify, then dilute into water.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.application: Spray weekly across the whole plant canopy, ensuring good leaf coverage on both sides.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.cause: Exserohilum turcicum fungus, thriving in moderate temperatures and prolonged wetness.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.symptoms: Long, cigar-shaped grayish-green lesions on leaves, which later turn tan and dry out.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.prevention_methods: Rotate crops with soybeans or alfalfa, perform deep tillage to bury crop debris, and manage drainage.

chemical_pesticides.name: Azoxystrobin + Propiconazole formulation
chemical_pesticides.safety_instructions: Toxic to fish and aquatic invertebrates. Do not spray within 30 days of harvest. Wear respirator.

fertilizer.application_timing: Apply at planting as basal dose, then side-dress at tassel formation.

Corn_(maize)___healthy.application: Plant appears healthy. Continue regular field monitoring and check irrigation.
Corn_(maize)___healthy.symptoms: Strong, upright stalk, vibrant green leaves with no long lesions or brown rust pustules.
Corn_(maize)___healthy.prevention_methods: Adopt broad crop rotation, manage corn borers, and perform soil checks.

chemical_pesticides.name: N/A (Not required)
chemical_pesticides.safety_instructions: None

fertilizer.application_timing: Apply in splits: 1/3 at sowing, 1/3 at knee-high, and 1/3 at tasseling.

Grape___Black_rot.preparation: Dissolve compounds in separate water containers, mix copper into lime while stirring.
Grape___Black_rot.application: Apply every 10-14 days starting at bud break until fruit set. Do not apply near harvest.
Grape___Black_rot.cause: Guignardia bidwellii fungus, overwintering in mummified berries and cane cankers.
Grape___Black_rot.symptoms: Small, circular tan spots on leaves, and berries that shrivel, turn hard, black, and resemble raisins.
Grape___Black_rot.prevention_methods: Prune vines to open the canopy to air, remove mummified grapes, keep vines tied off the ground.

chemical_pesticides.name: Mancozeb or Ziram or Myclobutanil
chemical_pesticides.safety_instructions: Highly toxic to fish. Do not apply directly to water. Wear respirator and goggles. Pre-harvest interval is 66 days for Mancozeb on grapes.

fertilizer.application_timing: In early spring just as shoots begin to emerge.

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).preparation: Mix Trichoderma and jaggery into water and allow to stand for 2 hours.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).application: Drench around root zones and paint pruning wounds with paste immediately after winter trimming.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).cause: Fhaeomoniella chlamydospora and Fomitiporia fungal complex entering through pruning wounds.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).symptoms: Tiger-stripe discoloration on leaves (interveinal yellow/brown necrosis), dark purple spotting on berries ('black measles'), and sudden vine apoplexy/wilting.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).prevention_methods: Disinfect pruning shears between vines with alcohol or bleach. Seal all large cuts with pruning paste.

chemical_pesticides.name: Fosetyl-Aluminium or Thiophanate-methyl paste
chemical_pesticides.safety_instructions: Wear chemical-resistant gloves. Do not apply during rain to allow sealant to dry.

fertilizer.quantity: 50 ml per vine diluted in water
fertilizer.application_timing: Apply in spring to stimulate new root formation and vascular healing.

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.preparation: Soak neem seed powder in water overnight, filter through a cloth, and add soap.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.application: Spray thoroughly on both upper and lower leaf surfaces every 10 days during warm humid weather.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.cause: Pseudocercospora vitis (Isariopsis clavispora) fungus, promoted by warm temperatures and frequent rains.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.symptoms: Irregular dark brown to black spots with yellowish halos on leaves, coalescing and causing premature defoliation.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.prevention_methods: Thin dense foliage to improve air circulation and sunlight. Clean dropped leaves post-harvest.

chemical_pesticides.name: Copper Oxychloride (COC) 50 WP
chemical_pesticides.safety_instructions: Wear safety goggles and gloves. Do not spray during hottest hours of the day. 14-day pre-harvest interval.

fertilizer.application_timing: Apply at fruit set stage.

Grape___healthy.application: Vines are healthy. Keep trellis pruned and tie loose canes.
Grape___healthy.cause: Optimal trellis ventilation and sun exposure
Grape___healthy.symptoms: Clear green fan-shaped leaves, firm green stems, healthy uniform grape clusters.
Grape___healthy.prevention_methods: Perform canopy thinning, maintain high trellis systems, and clean pruning tools.

chemical_pesticides.name: N/A (Not required)

fertilizer.quantity: 3 kg compost + 30g Epsom salts per vine
fertilizer.application_timing: Apply in early spring before flowering.

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).solution_name: Nutritional Zinc-Iron Foliar Boost & Neem Vector Spray
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).preparation: Dissolve micronutrients in water, emulsify neem oil with soap, and combine into solution.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).application: Spray trees every 14 days to suppress Asian Citrus Psyllid insect vectors and supplement deficient micronutrients.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).cause: Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus bacterium, transmitted by the Asian Citrus Psyllid (Diaphorina citri).
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).symptoms: Asymmetrical blotchy mottle on leaves, yellow shoots, small misshapen bitter green fruit that drops prematurely.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).prevention_methods: Plant only certified disease-free nursery stock. Control citrus psyllid vector vigorously using sticky traps and insecticidal sprays. Remove heavily declining trees.

chemical_pesticides.name: Imidacloprid or Thiamethoxam (for psyllid control)
chemical_pesticides.safety_instructions: Highly toxic to bees. NEVER spray during bloom. Wear respirator and protective garments.

fertilizer.fertilizer_type: Citrus Micronutrient Mix (Zn, Fe, Mn, B, Mg)
fertilizer.application_timing: Apply at new leaf flush periods 3 times per year.

Peach___Bacterial_spot.preparation: Mix copper hydroxide and lime into water thoroughly.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.application: Apply during dormant season and early spring before bud swell. Avoid high concentrations after bloom to prevent fruit russeting.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.cause: Xanthomonas arboricola pv. pruni bacteria, spreading via windblown rain in sandy soils.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small angular purple-black spots on leaves that drop out leaving a 'shot-hole' appearance. Pitted lesions on peaches.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.prevention_methods: Avoid planting susceptible cultivars in wind-exposed sandy sites. Plant windbreaks.

chemical_pesticides.name: Oxytetracycline or Copper octanoate
chemical_pesticides.safety_instructions: Do not exceed labeled seasonal limits. Wear mask and goggles. Pre-harvest interval is 21 days.

fertilizer.application_timing: Apply in early spring.

Peach___healthy.application: Peach tree is healthy. Maintain pruning and orchard floor weed control.
Peach___healthy.cause: Good orchard management and balanced drainage
Peach___healthy.symptoms: Vibrant lanceolate green leaves, smooth peach fruit, and sound bark.
Peach___healthy.prevention_methods: Thin fruit early in season. Apply copper spray at autumn leaf fall to prevent peach leaf curl.

chemical_pesticides.name: N/A (Not required)

fertilizer.quantity: 5 kg compost + 150g calcium nitrate per tree
fertilizer.application_timing: Apply in early spring before blossom.

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.preparation: Mix turmeric powder and copper formulation in water, add soap and shake vigorously.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.application: Apply every 7 days at the first sign of water-soaked spots. Best applied late afternoon.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.cause: Xanthomonas campestris pv. vesicatoria bacteria, seed-borne and rain-splashed.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, raised, wart-like spots on leaves and stems, turning brown; leaves turn yellow and drop off, exposing fruit to sunscald.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.prevention_methods: Use clean seeds, rotate crops, avoid working in the field when plants are wet, and destroy crop residues.

chemical_pesticides.name: Streptomycin Sulfate or Copper Hydroxide
chemical_pesticides.safety_instructions: Use antibiotic formulations only in severe cases. Wear protective face mask. Do not inhale spray mist.

fertilizer.application_timing: Apply as side-dressing when first fruits set to prevent blossom end rot.

Pepper,_bell___healthy.application: Pepper plant is healthy. Support with stakes if fruit load is heavy.
Pepper,_bell___healthy.cause: Good soil drainage and seed selection
Pepper,_bell___healthy.symptoms: Lustrous green leaves, sturdy stem branches, uniform blossoms, firm peppers.
Pepper,_bell___healthy.prevention_methods: Prune lower branches, apply straw mulch, and install drip irrigation.

Potato___Early_blight.preparation: Crush garlic and soak in oil for 24 hours. Strain, mix with water and soap.
Potato___Early_blight.application: Spray every 5 days on affected foliage, focusing on the undersides of leaves.
Potato___Early_blight.cause: Alternaria solani fungus, thriving when crops are stressed by poor nutrition or pests.
Potato___Early_blight.symptoms: Concentric dark brown rings on older leaves, forming leathery spots. Yield is reduced due to premature defoliation.
Potato___Early_blight.prevention_methods: Ensure optimal fertilizer application to prevent plant stress, rotate crops with non-solanaceous species.

chemical_pesticides.name: Difenoconazole or Chlorothalonil
chemical_pesticides.safety_instructions: Wear boots, protective clothing, and protective eyewear. Do not spray during peak sun hours to prevent leaf scorching.

fertilizer.application_timing: Incorporate thoroughly into soil before planting tubers.

Potato___Late_blight.preparation: Mix cow urine and neem oil into water, stir well, and let sit for 2-3 hours before use.
Potato___Late_blight.application: Spray thoroughly on foliage every week; also drench soil around roots monthly to strengthen plant defense.
Potato___Late_blight.cause: Phytophthora infestans, a highly destructive oomycete pathogen.
Potato___Late_blight.symptoms: Irregular dark green to black water-soaked lesions on leaves, white fungal bloom on undersides in humid conditions, and rotting tubers underground.
Potato___Late_blight.prevention_methods: Only plant certified seed potatoes, practice deep planting, destroy volunteer potato plants, and ensure proper hilling.

chemical_pesticides.name: Metalaxyl-M or Cymoxanil combined with Mancozeb
chemical_pesticides.safety_instructions: Extremely toxic if inhaled. Use respirator. Do not allow livestock to graze in sprayed fields for 3 weeks.

Soybean___healthy.cause: Proper Rhizobium inoculation and clean field cultivation
Soybean___healthy.symptoms: Trifoliate deep green leaves, sturdy stems, and uniform developing pods.
Soybean___healthy.prevention_methods: Practice 3-year crop rotation with corn or wheat. Manage aphids and leafhoppers.

Squash___Powdery_mildew.preparation: Mix baking soda, vegetable oil, and soap in water until completely emulsified.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.application: Spray thoroughly on both upper and lower leaf surfaces every 5-7 days at early sign of powdery mildew.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.cause: Podosphaera xanthii fungus, thriving in warm, dry weather with shaded foliage and high humidity.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White talcum-like powdery spots on leaf surfaces and petioles, leading to yellowing, browning, and leaf shriveling.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.prevention_methods: Plant in full sun with wide spacing. Water at the base with drip irrigation.

chemical_pesticides.name: Azoxystrobin or Trifloxystrobin
chemical_pesticides.safety_instructions: Rotate chemical modes of action to prevent fungal resistance. 3-day pre-harvest interval.

fertilizer.application_timing: Apply weekly to strengthen leaf epidermal resistance.

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.preparation: Dilute copper octanoate in clean water and mix well.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.application: Apply at early spring growth before blooms open, repeating every 10-14 days during wet conditions.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.cause: Diplocarpon earlianum fungus, spreading through splashing raindrops.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.symptoms: Small irregular purplish spots on upper leaf surfaces that enlarge and turn dark brown, giving the foliage a burnt or scorched appearance.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.prevention_methods: Plant on raised beds with straw mulch to prevent soil splashing. Remove old diseased leaves after harvest.

chemical_pesticides.name: Captan 50 WP or Pyraclostrobin
chemical_pesticides.safety_instructions: Wear rubber gloves. Do not apply during strawberry bloom to protect honeybees.

fertilizer.application_timing: Apply post-harvest after renovation.

Strawberry___healthy.application: Strawberry plants are healthy. Maintain straw mulching and monitor runner growth.
Strawberry___healthy.cause: Good soil drainage and clean mulch barrier
Strawberry___healthy.symptoms: Lush trifoliate green leaves, clean white flowers, and firm unblemished strawberries.
Strawberry___healthy.prevention_methods: Keep berries off bare soil using clean straw mulch. Ensure morning sun exposure.

chemical_pesticides.name: N/A (Not required)
chemical_pesticides.safety_instructions: None

fertilizer.application_timing: Apply around crown in early spring.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.preparation: Mix neem oil with soap to emulsify, dissolve turmeric powder in warm water, combine and shake well.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.application: Spray leaves thoroughly every 5-7 days; natural curcumin in turmeric inhibits bacterial proliferation.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.cause: Xanthomonas bacteria, carried on contaminated seed and splashed onto leaves by rain or irrigation.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, dark brown to black water-soaked spots on leaves with yellow halos, and scabby raised spots on green tomatoes.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.prevention_methods: Use certified pathogen-free seeds, avoid overhead sprinklers, and do not prune tomato plants when wet.

chemical_pesticides.dosage: 2g copper + 2g mancozeb per liter of water
chemical_pesticides.safety_instructions: Wear safety goggles and mask. Wash skin thoroughly after handling. Observe 7-day pre-harvest interval.

fertilizer.application_timing: Apply at early fruit set stage to strengthen cellular resistance.

Tomato___Early_blight.preparation: Crush garlic and chili, soak in water for 24 hours, strain through fine cloth, and mix in soap.
Tomato___Early_blight.application: Spray on infected plants every 4-5 days until symptoms subside, prioritizing lower leaves.
Tomato___Early_blight.cause: Alternaria solani fungus, surviving in soil debris and activated by warm, humid conditions.
Tomato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown spots with distinct concentric rings ('target-board' pattern) starting on older lower leaves, causing leaf yellowing and dieback.
Tomato___Early_blight.prevention_methods: Prune off bottom 12 inches of foliage to prevent soil splash. Mulch heavily with clean straw.

chemical_pesticides.name: Chlorothalonil or Azoxystrobin
chemical_pesticides.safety_instructions: Toxic to fish and bees. Wear protective gloves and eye protection. Do not spray in windy weather.

fertilizer.application_timing: Bi-weekly to support healthy vegetative regrowth.

Tomato___Late_blight.preparation: Mix baking soda, neem oil, and soap thoroughly into water until fully dissolved and emulsified.
Tomato___Late_blight.application: Spray on both sides of leaves every 5-7 days, ideally in late afternoon/evening to avoid leaf burn.
Tomato___Late_blight.cause: Phytophthora infestans oomycete pathogen, spreading rapidly during cool, wet, humid weather.
Tomato___Late_blight.symptoms: Large, dark water-soaked spots on leaves and stems, turning brown/black with white fuzzy fungal growth underneath in moist air.
Tomato___Late_blight.prevention_methods: Plant resistant cultivars, stake plants for airflow, destroy infected crop residues, and avoid overhead watering.

chemical_pesticides.name: Mancozeb or Metalaxyl-M fungicide
chemical_pesticides.safety_instructions: Wear full-body protective clothing. Keep away from water bodies. Observe 14-day pre-harvest interval.

fertilizer.fertilizer_type: High Potassium Organic Fertilizer (Wood ash or Kelp meal)
fertilizer.application_timing: Monthly to promote sturdy vascular systems and disease tolerance.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.preparation: Mix vinegar and baking soda in water slowly, then add soap as surfactant.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.application: Spray undersides of leaves where mold spores aggregate every 5-7 days.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.cause: Passalora fulva (Cladosporium fulvum) fungus, flourishing in greenhouse or humid outdoor conditions above 85% RH.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.symptoms: Pale greenish-yellow spots on upper leaf surfaces matching olive-green to brown velvety mold on leaf undersides.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.prevention_methods: Improve greenhouse ventilation. Space plants widely to facilitate air movement. Avoid wetting foliage.

chemical_pesticides.name: Copper Oxychloride or Difenoconazole
chemical_pesticides.safety_instructions: Wear respirator in enclosed spaces. Do not spray during high temperatures.

fertilizer.application_timing: At flowering stage.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.preparation: Soak compost in water for 24 hours, then strain thoroughly through a cloth.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.application: Spray weekly on affected foliage to boost beneficial microbes on leaf surfaces.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.cause: Septoria lycopersici fungus, favored by warm, wet, and humid conditions.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.symptoms: Numerous small, circular spots with dark brown margins and tan/gray centers, starting on lower leaves.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.prevention_methods: Mulch soil around plants, avoid overhead watering, rotate crops every 3 years, and remove lower diseased leaves.

chemical_pesticides.name: Chlorothalonil or Copper-based fungicides
chemical_pesticides.safety_instructions: Wear protective gloves and mask. Avoid spraying near bees. Do not harvest within 7 days of application.

fertilizer.application_timing: At flowering stage to support cellular wall strength and disease resistance.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.preparation: Emulsify neem oil and rosemary oil with castile soap in warm water.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.application: Spray vigorously focusing directly on leaf undersides where mites live. Apply every 3-4 days for two weeks.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.cause: Tetranychus urticae (Two-spotted spider mite), multiplying rapidly during hot, dry, dusty weather.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.symptoms: Fine yellow stippling or bronzing on leaves, delicate fine webbing between leaf stems, leaf desiccation, and premature drop.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.prevention_methods: Mist foliage periodically during hot dry spells to disrupt web building. Conserve predatory mites (Phytoseiidae).

chemical_pesticides.name: Abamectin or Spiromesifen Miticide
chemical_pesticides.safety_instructions: Highly toxic to beneficial insects. Apply in early morning before bees are active. 7-day pre-harvest interval.

fertilizer.quantity: 10 ml kelp + 5g Epsom salts per liter
fertilizer.application_timing: Foliar spray to help stressed plants recover chlorophyll.

Tomato___Target_Spot.preparation: Dissolve bicarbonate in water, emulsify neem oil with soap, and combine.
Tomato___Target_Spot.application: Spray foliage every 7 days as soon as circular target-like spots appear on leaves or stems.
Tomato___Target_Spot.cause: Corynespora cassiicola fungus, flourishing in warm, humid tropical and sub-tropical environments.
Tomato___Target_Spot.symptoms: Pinpoint water-soaked spots that enlarge into circular brown lesions with distinct pale centers and dark concentric rings.
Tomato___Target_Spot.prevention_methods: Increase spacing between plants to maximize airflow. Sanitize trellising stakes between seasons.

chemical_pesticides.name: Pyraclostrobin or Boscalid
chemical_pesticides.safety_instructions: Use protective gloves. Do not contaminate waterways. Pre-harvest interval is 7 days.

fertilizer.application_timing: Apply around root zone every 3 weeks.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.solution_name: Neem Oil & Yellow Sticky Trap Vector Management
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.preparation: Mix neem oil with soap in water. Place yellow sticky traps around the field perimeter at canopy height.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.application: Spray neem oil solution every 5 days on leaf undersides to deter whitefly vectors. Note: Virus itself has no cure; focus on vector control.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.cause: Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Begomovirus (TYLCV), transmitted exclusively by Silverleaf Whiteflies (Bemisia tabaci).
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.symptoms: Stunted bushy plants, severe upward curling and cupping of leaf margins, yellowing of leaf edges (chlorosis), and flower drop with negligible fruit set.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.prevention_methods: Use 50-mesh insect netting in greenhouses. Install yellow sticky traps. Immediately uproot and bag infected plants. Plant TYLCV-resistant hybrids.

chemical_pesticides.name: Spirotetramat or Cyantraniliprole (Whitefly insecticide)
chemical_pesticides.safety_instructions: Wear personal protective equipment. Toxic to bees. Do not apply during peak flowering.

fertilizer.fertilizer_type: Zinc and Magnesium sulfate foliar spray
fertilizer.application_timing: Apply to support uninfected neighbouring plants.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.preparation: Dissolve milk powder thoroughly in water. Milk proteins help deactivate viral particles on plant surfaces.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.application: Spray young seedlings and dip hands and pruning tools into milk solution before handling plants. Remove infected plants.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.cause: Tomato Mosaic Tobamovirus (ToMV), highly contagious and mechanically transmitted via hands, tools, and seeds.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.symptoms: Mottling of leaves with alternating light green and dark green patches, leaf blistering or 'shoestring' narrowing, and internal brown rings in fruit.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.prevention_methods: Wash hands with soap before touching plants. Do not smoke or use tobacco near tomato plants. Disinfect pruners with bleach.

chemical_pesticides.name: N/A (No chemical cures exist for viral infections)
chemical_pesticides.dosage: None - disinfect tools with 10% household bleach
chemical_pesticides.safety_instructions: Uproot infected plants, bag them, and destroy away from the field. Do not compost.

fertilizer.application_timing: Apply to enhance systemic vigour in remaining healthy plants.

Tomato___healthy.application: Plant appears healthy. Continue regular monitoring, balanced watering, and crop hygiene.
Tomato___healthy.symptoms: Dark green leaves, robust stems, no lesions or abnormal spot patterns.
Tomato___healthy.prevention_methods: Crop rotation, clean equipment, well-draining soil, weed management.

chemical_pesticides.name: N/A (Not required)
chemical_pesticides.safety_instructions: None

fertilizer.application_timing: At vegetative growth stage (every 4 weeks)

_default.preparation: Mix neem oil with soap to emulsify, then dilute in water thoroughly.
_default.application: Spray weekly on all foliage as a general-purpose organic preventive treatment. Consult a local agricultural expert for disease-specific advice.
_default.cause: General agricultural pathogens (fungi, bacteria, or virus)
_default.symptoms: Leaf spots, discoloration, wilting, curling, or abnormal structural growth.
_default.prevention_methods: Practice clean weeding, crop rotation, and avoid overhead watering.

chemical_pesticides.name: Broad-spectrum Chlorothalonil or Mancozeb
chemical_pesticides.safety_instructions: Wear complete protective gear. Do not spray within 7-14 days of harvesting. Keep away from domestic animals.

fertilizer.fertilizer_type: Balanced NPK (19-19-19) or Organic Humic Acid
fertilizer.application_timing: Apply during active growth periods every 20-30 days.
